prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin for [choose_path, redesign], [finish, new_flow], [finish, new_screen], [sign_in, notification], and [sign_in, reorder] as each category has only one test.
[finish, redesign] changes can be helpful, as two of five tests won (+5.5% and +4.3% after noise correction), while three showed no clear effect.
Evidence for [adoption, new_flow] and [adoption, new_screen] remains mixed: for each category, one test won while the others showed no clear effect.
Evidence for [adoption, redesign] remains inconsistent across four tests: one won (+5.5% after noise correction), two were worse or stopped early (-8.3% and -4.0%), and one showed no clear effect.
Predictions were consistently too low for all winning tests.
Predictions were usually too high for tests that stopped early, lost, or showed no clear effect.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, new_flow: +0.4% after noise correction, 3 test(s)
- adoption, new_screen: +1.9% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- adoption, redesign: -1.1% after noise correction, 4 test(s)
- choose_path, redesign: +3.2% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_flow: +9.9% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_screen: -6.8% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, redesign: +1.2% after noise correction, 5 test(s)
- sign_in, notification: +1.0% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: -8.2% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 74.0%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 83.7%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 28.0%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [adoption, new_screen] Pet Arrival Ritual Screen: Introduce a dedicated celebration screen right after pet choice to perform an interactive pet adoption ritual before printing the certificate. (why: Adoption step drops 26% of users and takes 89s median / 1017s mean. Adding a clear ritual milestone builds user investment and momentum.)
1: [sign_in, notification] Sign In Account Sync Status Banner: Display an explicit cloud sync reassurance notification on the sign-in screen informing returning users that their adopted pets will automatically restore. (why: 8 support emails complained about missing or reset pets after signing in again, making account confidence a major churn risk.)
2: [adoption, wait_info] Custom Pet Generation Status Tracker: Add explicit estimated generation times and photo processing status feedback on the photo upload screen. (why: 3 support tickets reported custom pet generation failures or weird results. Clear visual expectations prevent premature exit during photo processing.)
3: [finish, hint] Desktop Pet Quick Shortcut Hint: Add a dedicated tray icon tip and hotkey summary banner on the finish screen. (why: Support messages show confusion on how to hide, control, or converse with pets once onboarding completes.)
4: [home, notification] Desktop Pet Launch Notification Prompt: Enable desktop readiness notifications on the waiting screen so users are alerted when pet initialization finishes. (why: Home waiting step has a median time of 201s and mean time of 2336s. Notifications keep users engaged if rendering takes longer.)

scores.note: Target step drops 26% of users, but introducing a new screen requires high engineering effort and adoption screen history is mixed.
8 support emails directly highlight account sync anxiety at sign in, though historical evidence for sign-in notifications remains thin.
Adoption has high drop-off and very long completion times; support tickets confirm user confusion during photo generation.
Finish step already converts well at 83.7%, but UI tip is low cost and addresses explicit post-onboarding support complaints.
Home wait step has extreme wait times (201s median / 2336s mean); desktop notifications help re-engage users when ready.
